stories.headline: NDA seals YSRCP’s fate in rural local body polls by winning 499 ZPTC and 5,861 MPTC seats
stories.deck: State Election Commission set the stage for elections to Gram Panchayats in three phases i.e on November 26 and 29 and December 2, for which the Commission will issue notifications on November 13, 16 and 19
stories.bodyText:
The NDA partners TDP, Jana Sena Party (JSP) and BJP sealed the YSR Congress Party (YSRCP)’s fate in the elections to 582 Zilla Parishad Territorial Constituencies (ZPTCs) by winning 499 (TDP 406, JSP 73 and BJP 20) seats confining the YSRCP to 76 seats.
In the elections to 7,768 Mandal Parishad Territorial Constituencies (MPTCs), TDP won 4,806, JSP 938 and BJP 117 (total 5,861). YSRCP won 1,711 MPTCs, CPI (M) 15, Congress 9 and Bhajuan Samaj Party 3.
Gram Panchayat polls from Nov. 26
Meanwhile, the State Election Commission set the stage for elections to Gram Panchayats in three phases i.e on November 26 and 29 and December 2, for which the Commission will issue notifications on November 13, 16 and 19.
The SEC announced the lifting of the Model Code of Conduct (MCC) in 100 Urban Local Bodies (Municipal Corporations and Municipalities) following the completion of elections to them. However, the MCC is in force in the rural areas where elections are due on the given dates.

stories.headline: Deepavali 2026: All you need to know about Supreme Court-permitted time slots, green crackers and other directives
stories.deck: The Supreme Court permitted the bursting of certified green firecrackers between 6 a.m. and 7 a.m. and between 8 p.m. and 10 p.m. on November 7 and November 8, 2026 in Delhi-NCR
stories.bodyText:
The Supreme Court on November 2, 2026 described bursting of firecrackers during Deepavali as a “religious practice” while permitting the use of green firecrackers for two days, on November 7 and November 8, in Delhi-NCR.
The unregulated use of firecrackers during Deepavali has historically led to a sharp rise in the Air Quality Index (AQI) and pollution levels, including the emission of particulate matter, the court observed. “The right of an individual to engage in a particular practice, which may have a religious colour, is only a qualified one and cannot go beyond the Constitutional restrictions,” the Supreme Court held.
Failure of the state
The state had “utterly failed” to comply with the Supreme Court’s orders issued since 2015 to impose restrictions on fireworks, the Bench said. In fact, the situation had not improved even after the reimposition of a complete ban on firecrackers. A significant spike in AQI levels was noticed on Dasara and the following day. The “complete ban” had not only facilitated the illegal sale of firecrackers but had also prevented people from purchasing authorised green crackers, the court said.
The court had earlier suggested that the government enlist celebrities such as cricketer Virat Kohli to spread awareness about the harmful effects of firecrackers.
In October 2025, the apex court had permitted the sale and bursting of green firecrackers in Delhi-NCR during Deepavali, subject to conditions aimed at balancing tradition with environmental and health concerns. The court had then made it clear that the use of green crackers would be restricted to specified hours on the festival day and its eve.
Time slots to burst crackers
The court permitted the bursting of certified green firecrackers between 6 a.m. and 7 a.m. and between 8 p.m. and 10 p.m. on November 7, 2026 and the day after in the Delhi National Capital Region (Delhi-NCR).
“There shall not be any bursting of fireworks within a 300-metre radius of hospitals, nursing homes, primary and district health centres, old age homes and any notified silence zones. These areas will be declared as ‘no-cracker zones’, and shall be marked on the ground and published,” the court said in its 23-page order. The same restriction would apply to educational institutions.
“We are conscious that the celebration of Deepavali has a religious, social, psychological and emotional connotation amongst people, creating a positive atmosphere of hope, welfare and prosperity. That being said, allowing the environment to degrade, which results in a health hazard to all living beings, defeats the very purpose of the festivities, and the celebrations would be rendered nugatory,” the Bench reasoned.
Directions on green firecrackers
In a series of directions, the court ordered that only manufacturers certified by CSIR-NEERI (Council of Scientific and Industrial Research-National Environmental Engineering Research Institute) and PESO (Petroleum and Explosives Safety Organisation) would be permitted to manufacture green crackers between November 2, 2026 and November 6, 2026. The cracker boxes would be sealed and kept separate from unauthorised or conventional firecrackers.
There would be no manufacture or sale of firecrackers joined in series (ladis) and garlands. Only firecrackers carrying product-specific QR codes would be allowed to be sold. Cancelled licences of traders would be restored temporarily from November 4, 2026 to November 6, 2026. Manufacturers and traders of firecrackers in Delhi-NCR must furnish a monetary security deposit, the amount of which would be determined by the authorities.
What are green firecrackers?
Green firecrackers are designed to cause less air pollution. According to the CSIR-National Environmental Engineering Research Institute (NEERI) team that developed them, these firecrackers emit 30% less particulate matter or, alternatively, 20% less particulate matter and 10% fewer gaseous emissions than conventional firecrackers in the same category.
The proportions of fuels and oxidisers have been modified to improve combustion efficiency, additives have been introduced to suppress dust formation, and the quantities of certain metals have been reduced.
CSIR-NEERI has developed three types of green firecrackers: Safe Water Releaser (SWAS), whose ingredients release water vapour to suppress some of the particulate matter generated during combustion; Safe Thermite Cracker (STAR), which uses a thermite-based composition to achieve higher combustion efficiency and lower emissions; and Safe Minimal Aluminium (SAFAL), which contains less aluminium and consequently generates lower emissions.
Restrictions on sale of uncertified crackers
Each of SWAS, STAR and SAFAL type of green firecrackers can be used in different types of fireworks, including sparklers and flowerpots.
All green firecracker products carry a CSIR-NEERI logo on their packaging and a QR code to verify the product certification. While they produce lower emissions than conventional crackers, they are not pollution-free. Their emissions include fine particulate matter, harmful gases and other combustion by-products that affect respiratory and cardiovascular health. They also generate noise pollution.
The sale of green firecrackers will be permitted from November 4 to November 6, while bursting will be allowed only on November 7, 2026 and November 8, 2026 between 6 a.m. and 7 a.m. and between 8 p.m. and 10 p.m., according to the Delhi Police. Firecrackers joined in series (ladis), and crackers containing prohibited chemicals such as barium salts will not be permitted.

stories.headline: Amravati auto-driver wins hearts with fluent English and big dreams
stories.deck: An elderly auto-rickshaw driver from Amravati has captured hearts with his impressive command of English. A viral video shows him eloquently discussing travel abroad, inspiring many locals who fondly call him Yadav Chacha. His infectious cheer and remarkable communication skills have drawn comparisons to prominent figures, highlighting how language can bridge gaps and create new opportunities for…
stories.bodyText:
'If you know English, you can go to London, Paris, America'. These are the words going viral on social media these days. Also a perfect example of the fact that sometimes, the most memorable lessons come from the most unexpected people. A video from 2024 has resurfaced showing an auto-rickshaw driver from Amravati, Maharashtra, speaking fluent English.
In a world where English is often judged with formal education and corporate offices, this elderly auto driver's brilliant English and confidence have caught the internet's attention. The man is not just showing off his language skills but also encouraging others to learn the language.
The viral video
The video shows the driver in conversation with a young man while a passenger sits inside his auto-rickshaw. His confidence is contagious. He clearly explains why learning English matters and is important.
The video was shared by Instagram user Bhushan Pohane (@kon_bhushan1222), who admitted that he was taken by surprise by the driver's fluency.
He captioned the video:
“Even I was stunned and stuttered a bit , while speaking to him to my surprise, seeing his fluency in English”.
'If you know English, you can go to London, Paris, America'
The conversation begins with the driver making it clear that he has something important to say. In a confident voice, he tells the young man,
"What I am telling you, listen to me very carefully. If you know English, you can go to London, Paris, America. 
If you don't know English, you cannot go there."
He then goes on to explain why English is useful when travelling abroad. Giving the example of visiting a hotel in London, he says that someone who knows English can comfortably ask a waiter for a glass of water and communicate their needs. However, if the same request is made in Marathi, the waiter might not understand.
He further says, "That is why I am telling you, you learn English, you talk in English. It is an international language".
Who is the auto driver everyone is talking about?
Interestingly, the man appears to be more than just someone who knows how to speak English. Many residents of Amravati affectionately call him as 'Yadav Chacha'.
One commenter shared that the driver's auto-rickshaw had been parked outside their house for years and that they had known him for a long time.
The person described him as a hardworking, kind, friendly and fun-loving gentleman who had experienced considerable struggles in life. They also mentioned that he regularly greeted people in English, from good morning to good evening.
Social media is in love with Yadav Chacha
Indian auto (Canva)
As expected, the internet had plenty to say about the elderly man's impressive communication skills.
Several users praised his English, with one commenting that the driver's language skills were better than theirs despite having spent 16 years in formal education. Another compared the way he spoke to former Indian President and renowned scientist Dr APJ Abdul Kalam.
Others appreciated his cheerful personality and beautiful smile. One viewer even expressed hope that the video would reach the right people and help the gentleman receive the recognition he deserved.

stories.headline: Iraq has reached understandings with US to allow oil exports through Hormuz: Minister
stories.bodyText: Iraq has reached understandings with the United States to allow Iraqi oil exports through the Strait of Hormuz via a shipping lane near Oman, Foreign Minister Fuad Hussein said in an interview with Al Jazeera. He said Iraq's losses from the Iran war and disruptions to oil exports had reached $60 billion. .Iran exempts ships from India, China, Qatar from transit restrictions in Strait of Hormuz. Iraq's oil exports recovered in October after a sharp drop the previous month. Exports rose to about 3.5 million barrels per day from 2.65 million bpd in September, according to Iraqi energy officials.

stories.headline: Trump says he is highly unlikely to order Iran strikes if talks progress
stories.bodyText: Washington: US President Donald Trump on Sunday said he was highly unlikely to order fresh attacks on Iran as long as talks to end the conflict progress, even as both countries reported that shipping had been hit in or near the Strait of Hormuz. "It depends on whether or not they sign a very strong agreement," Trump told CNN in a phone interview. "The answer is, highly unlikely it's going to be necessary." CNN did not specify exactly what it had asked Trump, who also said that if strikes resume, the US has identified potential infrastructure targets, including 38 bridges "that we can knock down in literally one hour." Trump had hinted at renewing major attacks on Iran after last week's US midterm elections, but there has been no sign of a large-scale US military operation. Iran has said it would respond by striking US and Israeli targets. Iranian media suggested that explosions in southern Iran on Saturday were related to Iranian military activities rather than US strikes. Iran's state television said officials had not confirmed any missile strikes on Iranian territory following blasts heard in several areas, including on Qeshm Island in the strait. .Tankers hit in Hormuz as Iran keeps up pressure after US vote. Both the US and Iran have continued strikes on vessels in the Strait of Hormuz, however, restricting exports of energy and other commodities vital to the world economy. Iran's state television said the evening explosions might be related to Iranian military activity in the waterway, where Iran said two vessels had hit mines and a third had caught fire. The US said its air force had disabled a vessel in the Gulf of Oman beyond the strait. Tasnim news agency said two missiles had struck Qeshm Island, with no official information on possible damage. Neither Iran nor the US has commented on that report. Washington said on November 2 that it had struck the island in a limited defensive measure against Iranians using surface-to-air missiles against US assets. COMMERCIAL VESSEL, OIL TANKERS HIT Since the US and Israel began attacks on Iran in February, Tehran has sought the upper hand by hitting vessels in the Strait of Hormuz to block Gulf energy exports, while US forces began blockading movements to and from Iranian ports in April. The US military said on Saturday evening that its air force had fired at the stern of a commercial vessel in the Gulf of Oman, disabling it as it tried to get through the blockade. .Iran says it would reopen Strait of Hormuz in 2 days as part of US deal. Iran's Revolutionary Guards Navy said two oil tankers had caught fire after hitting mines while attempting to pass through an "unauthorized route" in the Strait of Hormuz. A third tanker had also suffered an explosion and caught fire, the semi-official Fars news agency reported later. Reuters was not able to confirm any of the reported strikes. Monitors from the United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations said a bulk carrier and military forces were involved in an incident in the Gulf of Oman, approximately 18 nautical miles east of the United Arab Emirates' city of Khor Fakkan, with damage unknown. It was unclear if it was related to the reported US attack. SAUDI STATE OIL COMPANY BUILDING DAMAGED A conflict between Iran-aligned Houthis in Yemen and Saudi Arabia has escalated this month, enlarging the wider Middle East war. On Sunday, Saudi Arabia's energy ministry said an administrative building belonging to state oil company Saudi Aramco in Riyadh had been damaged by falling debris after an attempted attack, with no injuries or fatalities reported. Qatar, which has been mediating in talks to try to end the conflict that has shaken the world economy, on Saturday denied reports that the US and Iran had failed to reach a deal. The Qatari prime minister had affirmed that both sides were continuing to work toward an agreement, it said. Iran has submitted a nuclear proposal to Washington through Qatar, a senior Iranian official told Reuters on Thursday, saying the US was reviewing it but discussions would depend on Washington first meeting Tehran's seven demands. These include sanctions relief, access to frozen assets and war reparations, while Washington insists nuclear issues must feature in initial talks. On Saturday, the US military said it was launching a task force to crack down on the movement of advanced weapons and other sanctioned material to Iran via its land borders and the Caspian Sea — part of economic measures to try to pressure Tehran. Iran's Revolutionary Guards dismissed the plan as "wordplay," saying it would not work because Tehran had made preparations and communicated closely with its neighbours.

briefs.headline: Major fire breaks out in Mumbai's Dongri, dousing ops on; one dead in November 7 highrise blaze
briefs.deck: The Mumbai Fire Brigade (MFB) declared it a Level-I fire call at 10.11 p.m., deploying a large number of its personnel along with those from the police, BEST, ward and 108 ambulance service for dousing operations
briefs.bodyText:
A major fire broke out in Mumbai's Dongri area late Sunday (November 8, 2026) night, engulfing several shops and hutments, civic officials and residents said.
The fire broke out at Haji Kasam Chawl, near Datta Mandir, on Dr Maheshwari Road, and spread across a large area.
While residents also reported hearing loud "explosion-like" sounds, it could not be independently confirmed.
The Mumbai Fire Brigade (MFB) declared it a Level-I fire call at 10.11 p.m., deploying a large number of its personnel along with those from the police, BEST, ward and 108 ambulance service for dousing operations.
"Efforts to bring the blaze under control are underway. Further details about the extent of damage and possible casualties are awaited," an official said.
In another incident, a fire broke out at Kamgar Stadium in Dr. Babasaheb Ambedkar Nagar in Dadar West at around 10.15 a.m. on Sunday (November 8).
The blaze, involving wooden and bamboo materials, was extinguished by the fire brigade at 10.32 a.m. No injuries were reported, an official said.
Meanwhile, a person was killed in a fire that broke out at a highrise residential building in Lokhandwala in Andheri West on Saturday (November 7) night, officials said.

Police raid home of ex-President of Paraguay
briefs.deck: Santiago Pena is accused of steering millions in government deposits to Ueno Bank and concealing its financial troubles despite warnings about loans and solvency
briefs.bodyText:
Police in Paraguay raided the home of ex-president Santiago Pena as part of a probe into a banking crisis that triggered his dismissal from office and criminal charges against him.
Authorities last week intervened to seize Ueno Bank, a popular online lender that held accounts for nearly half of Paraguay’s 6.5 million people, plus more than $800 million in government funds.
Its collapse rocked this small, normally stable country, leading to street protests. Mr. Pena is now being held in custody at a military facility.
Mr. Pena, who came to power in 2023, owned shares in the bank’s holding company, Ueno Holding, until he sold them last year.
He is accused of using his influence as president to steer millions in government deposits to Ueno Bank and of hiding or downplaying its financial woes even though he was warned about questionable loans and solvency issues.
Prosecutors announced in a statement that Mr. Pena’s home was raided as part of the probe into the bank collapse.
They say Ueno Bank received deposits from government entities even as it granted questionable loans to companies linked to Ueno executives.
Mr. Pena’s mansion outside Asuncion is part of the probe. The indictment says that in 2024 he received two loans from Ueno Bank totalling around $500,000 so he could build the house.
His monthly mortgage payment is $38,000 -- six times his monthly salary as president, the charging sheet says.
The Senate voted on Friday (November 6, 2026) to dismiss Mr. Pena, and Vice-President Pedro Alliana took his place.
Mr. Alliana said Sunday (November 8, 2026) the government has reimbursed 1.2 million Ueno Bank customers whose money was frozen in the collapse.
The disbursal totals around $158 million so far, and it will continue this week, he said.

briefs.headline: Nvidia investigating reports that CEO Jensen Huang was targeted by Chinese intelligence
briefs.deck: The announcement came after Jensen Huang acknowledged to the board that he had been intimate with a business executive whom U.S. intelligence determined was gathering information for Beijing
briefs.bodyText:
Nvidia is opening an investigation into reports that CEO Jensen Huang was the “target of a foreign intelligence effort,” the company's board of directors said Sunday (November 8, 2026).
The announcement came after Mr. Huang acknowledged to the board that he had been intimate with a business executive whom U.S. intelligence determined was gathering information for Beijing, The New York Times reported.
Mr. Huang apologised in a message to the company, according to the Times. “I was unfaithful to my wife,” he said. “My actions hurt her and our children. There is no excuse for what I did. I am deeply sorry.”
Nvidia's board said in a statement it has “no reason to believe that either national security or Nvidia secrets were compromised,” but that its inquiry would examine all available information. Mr. Huang “fully supports the review and has committed to cooperating with it,” the board said.
Mr. Huang, 63, will remain CEO during the investigation.
The Times reported last month that U.S. intelligence agencies had discovered that Mr. Huang had developed a close relationship with Alice Huang, a Chinese citizen and chip buyer, and determined that she was feeding information directly to Beijing. The two are not related, according to the Times.
Ms. Alice Huang was previously a television reporter in China before becoming a top executive at Singapore-based data centre company Megaspeed, which has become one of Nvidia's biggest customers in Southeast Asia. Megaspeed bought more than $4.8 billion worth of Nvidia chips over the past two years, according to the Times.

briefs.headline: G7 Ministers meet on efforts to end Ukraine conflict, halt new Iran war
briefs.deck: Ministers from the leading industrialised nations of Britain, Canada, France, Germany, Italy, Japan and the United States will be gathering with preoccupations strikingly similar to those of the last such meeting in March
briefs.bodyText:
Foreign Ministers of the G7 group meet in Paris from Monday (November 9, 2026) for two days of talks expected to see European powers press the United States to seek a fair settlement for Ukraine in the war against Russia and deter Washington from further military action against Iran.
Ministers from the leading industrialised nations of Britain, Canada, France, Germany, Italy, Japan and the United States will be gathering with preoccupations strikingly similar to those of the last such meeting in March.
Russia’s war against Ukraine following the February 2022 full-scale invasion of its neighbour is grinding towards its fifth anniversary. And Washington is still not ruling out new attacks against Iran even after the defeat of President Donald Trump’s Republicans in the midterms.
All eyes will be on U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio who is due to attend both days, unlike the March meeting where he only came for one.
This G7 ministerial meeting, one of the final acts of the French G7 presidency that saw President Emmanuel Macron host Donald Trump for the leaders’ summit this summer in the lakeside resort of Evian, had long been scheduled to be held in the southern port city of Marseille.
But at the last minute the event was moved to Paris, with only scheduling reasons given for the change.
The visit by Mr. Rubio — seen by U.S. media as a potential candidate to succeed Mr. Trump — will be his first abroad since the midterms. Washington will also in 2027 take over the G7 presidency from France.
‘Europeans will be represented’
The meeting coincides with U.S.-mediated talks with Moscow and Kyiv in Abu Dhabi scheduled for Tuesday (November 10, 2026) and Wednesday (November 11, 2026) on ending the Ukraine war, with Europe concerned Kyiv must not be forced to accept disadvantageous conditions.
French Foreign Minister Jean-Noel Barrot told RTL radio that on this occasion “Europeans will be represented and France will be in Abu Dhabi to participate in these talks”.
Mr. Trump stoked fears of a U.S. pivot toward the Kremlin by predicting a “very big” deal with Russia involving not only the Ukraine war but “all of Europe”.
Jared Kushner, the U.S. President’s envoy and son-in-law, said the United States was working on “a broader European security architecture that can help establish the conditions for lasting peace”, a concept met with scepticism in the past by Europe.
On Iran, Mr. Trump has not ruled out new strikes, including at so-called Pickaxe Mountain, a suspected nuclear site which Tehran denies is such a facility. Europeans, however, are eager to see a resolution and shipping traffic return to normal in the Strait of Hormuz energy transit hub.
“We’re dealing with them now,” Mr. Trump said of the Iranians on Friday (November 6, 2026). “They want to make a deal very badly.”
The sidelines of the meeting will also see the French Finance Ministry hosting on Monday (November 9, 2026) a donor conference to raise funds to repair the dome protecting the nuclear reactor that exploded in Ukraine’s Chernobyl in 1986 after it was damaged in a Russian strike last year.
Around 500 million euros is required but only just over half has been raised so far with a target date of spring 2027 to muster the rest of the funds, the French finance ministry told AFP.
Even though the meeting was moved to Paris, Marseille will still host the launch of a network of 14 global ports uniting to combat drug trafficking, which has become a major scourge in the southern city, Barrot said.
As he addressed reporters while preparing to leave for France, Rubio declined to comment directly on Mr. Trump’s and the Republicans’ crushing loss in the U.S. midterm elections.
“It is not uncommon to have a division of power in this country,” Mr. Rubio told reporters, alluding to the fact that Trump will now see both houses of Congress controlled by the Democrats.
Asked about widespread protests in France, Rubio added that he was not worried and trusted U.S. counterparts on the ground who advised him it is safe to attend the G7 meeting.
Published - November 09, 2026 07:35 am IST

briefs.headline: 19 Indian seafarers stranded in Yemen evacuated, Embassy says
briefs.deck: The evacuation comes days after India said 14 Indian nationals aboard a yacht involved in an incident off the Yemeni coast were safe
briefs.bodyText:
Nineteen Indian seafarers stranded in Yemen's Hodeidah and Sana'a for the past two weeks have been evacuated, with all of them safe and on their way back to their country, the Indian Embassy in Yemen said on Sunday (November 8, 2026).
“All seafarers are safe, in good health, and on their way back to India. The Embassy sincerely thanks all concerned for their valuable cooperation and continued support in facilitating the safe evacuation of our Indian nationals,” the mission said in a post on X.
Also Read | All 14 Indians in yacht incident off Yemen coast reported safe: Embassy
The evacuation comes days after India said 14 Indian nationals aboard a yacht involved in an incident off the Yemeni coast were safe.
It is not immediately clear whether the 14 are among the 19 seafarers evacuated.
On October 23, the Indian mission had said all 14 Indian nationals aboard a yacht near Hodeidah were safe and that it was in contact with relevant parties to establish the circumstances surrounding the incident.
Some Arab media outlets had earlier quoted spokesperson Yahya Saree of the Yemen-based Houthi group as claiming that Saudi forces targeted the Indian yacht near Yuqar Island in the Red Sea, close to the Yemeni coast.
Mr. Saree had said the yacht was carrying 14 Indian nationals and that Houthi forces were rescuing them.
The incident came amid renewed escalation between Saudi Arabia and Yemen's Houthis, with attacks and counterattacks reported in recent days.
Saudi Arabia has intercepted Houthi missiles and drones, while Saudi-led coalition forces have carried out airstrikes in Yemen, raising fears of a return to wider conflict after relative calm under a 2022 truce.
The latest violence has also affected civilian and energy infrastructure and heightened concerns over security in the Red Sea and the Bab al-Mandab Strait, a key international shipping route.

Pope Leo takes Milei to task as he visits divided Argentina
briefs.deck: Pope Leo spoke out in defence of the poor and pensioners, insisting that “particular concern be shown for those affected by illness, dependency and disability” — a veiled reference to the government’s controversial cuts to disability assistance
briefs.bodyText:
Pope Leo XIV delivered a stinging critique of Argentina President Javier Milei's harsh austerity measures on Sunday (November 8, 2026), insisting growth must benefit all in a speech met with rapturous applause.
"The economy must be at the service of the people, rather than people being at the service of the economy," he said, shortly after landing in Argentina on the second leg of a Latin America tour.
Pope Leo stressed the plight of those who, "despite hard work, nonetheless struggle to meet their household's needs."
He spoke out in defence of the poor and pensioners, insisting that "particular concern be shown for those affected by illness, dependency and disability" — a veiled reference to the government's controversial cuts to disability assistance.
And he told Mr. Milei, known for his foul-mouthed diatribes, that strengthening democracy required a "willingness to listen" and the "careful use of words."
The visit is the first by a pontiff to Argentina in nearly four decades and Pope Leo was met with calls to help mend deep divisions in the country after three years of austerity under Mr. Milei.
Pope Leo arrived in Buenos Aires from Uruguay, where he began his first trip to Latin America as Pope, the world's most Catholic continent that is becoming increasingly secular.
The visit is the first by a pontiff to the home country of the late Pope Francis in nearly four decades.
Mr. Milei famously insulted Pope Francis for his pro-poor teachings. Pope Leo said he was "retracing" Pope Francis's steps.
‘Unite us’
Argentines are hoping the leader of the world's 1.4 billion Catholics will help unite the country, which is bitterly divided between supporters and opponents of Mr. Milei.
"Just like the World Cup unites us, hopefully the Pope will too," said Liliana Deblauwe, a 68-year-old retired teacher who waited with hundreds of people to see the Pope visit a monument to liberation hero Jose de San Martin.
Hundreds more chanting "Papa Leon" (Spanish for Leo) gathered outside the presidential palace, where he was hosted by Mr. Milei.
Brian Inacio Rodriguez, a 26-year-old job seeker, spent five days travelling overland from Ushuaia, at the very tip of South America, to see the pontiff. He said he hoped he brought "much peace to Argentina."
Just three weeks after undergoing surgery for lung cancer, Pope Leo is on an ambitious 12-day tour of the continent where he served nearly two decades as a missionary.
In Uruguay, he condemned drug violence and urged an end to child poverty.
The Argentine stage of his visit aims to boost the flagging faith of a country left disappointed by Pope Francis's failure to visit during his papacy. It will also act as a litmus test of support for the Church. Some 57.7% of people identified as Catholic in a recent University of Buenos Aires poll, down from around 90% in the 1960s.
Pope Leo will visit a home for disabled people and a prison and celebrate three open-air masses. The Church has said it expects a total of seven million faithful at the various events.
‘Imbecile’ Francis
Mr. Milei came to office on a promise to revive Argentina's ailing economy and tame runaway inflation by shrinking the welfare state, targeting public hospitals, universities and pensioners in particular.
The poverty rate has swung wildly since he came to power — increasing to 32.3% in September.
A close ally of U.S. President Donald Trump, with a similar combative style, Mr. Milei had a tense relationship with Pope Francis.
On the campaign trail the cost-cutting economist called his countryman an "imbecile" for championing social justice.
Once in office, however, he softened his tone but he continues to heap insults on the press and opposition.
His relationship with Pope Leo has so far been cordial, but the local Catholic Church has heavily criticised him for treating key social services solely as a budgetary constraint.
Mr. Milei has also been criticised for restricting several democratic freedoms, including the right to protest. But he maintains a loyal supporter base for drastically reducing inflation.
Published - November 09, 2026 05:08 am IST

stories.headline: '3-month North India tour': How Bengaluru serial killer forced boy to send voice messages to conceal parents' murder
stories.deck: A 10-year-old boy was coerced by Indushekhar, the alleged killer of his parents. He was instructed to say his parents were away on a pilgrimage. The boy recorded misleading messages on his parents' phones while becoming suspicious of a foul odor in Indushekhar's car. Indushekhar had driven the boy to Nandi Hills, discarding heavy gunny bags during the journey.
stories.bodyText:
BENGALURU: For five days after his parents went missing, the 10-year-old son of the murdered couple Shankar and Nalini was made to tell relatives and family friends that they were away on a pilgrimage and later on a three-month North India tour.
The messages were not his own.
Police said the boy told them that alleged killer Indushekhar dictated what he should say and made him record voice messages using mobile phones belonging to his parents and others.
According to the boy's statement, his father went missing on a Saturday morning, and his mother was nowhere to be found by afternoon. Indushekhar came to pick him up that evening, saying they would go on a pilgrimage.
Police said the child trusted Indushekhar because he was a familiar person and had ties with the family. The boy told them that Indushekhar did not allow him to speak directly to relatives.
Instead, he handed him the phones and made him record voice messages. Initially, he was instructed to say his parents were at a temple and had handed their phones to people there.
"He told me to say they were going on a North India tour for three more months and no one should bother them," police quoted the boy as having said.
The child also recalled a foul smell inside Indushekhar's car during the period. The boy noticed two or three heavy gunny bags in the vehicle and asked the accused about the stench. Indushekhar allegedly dismissed his questions, saying there were waste materials in the back.
When he tried to look inside the bags, Indushekhar allegedly scolded him and warned him against going near them. Indushekhar later drove towards Nandi Hills and threw the sacks away.

stories.headline: Karnataka CM: Ethanol probe covered blending units; findings today
stories.bodyText:
BENGALURU: Karnataka
 chief minister 
DK Shivakumar
 Sunday asserted that investigations into excessive ethanol blend — more than 30% against the prescribed 20% — in fuel stations in the state were comprehensive and covered processing units where the fuel and the chemical are blended.
Stating that the Centre cannot shirk its responsibility as public safety is paramount, the CM said food and civil supplies minister Rizwan Arshad will release a detailed report on Monday with documentary evidence on how and where the blend is done.
“It is not right to increase the blending ratio just to profit from ethanol available at a lower cost. The govt has taken the issue seriously,” he said, adding information has been shared with the Union govt.
BJP state president BY Vijayendra challenged the state govt to disclose the standards it followed while testing petrol samples for ethanol blending and cooperate with oil-marketing companies in conducting joint tests to establish the facts.
He said Indian Oil, Bharat Petroleum and Hindustan Petroleum had issued clarifications following the state govt’s claim that ethanol content in petrol samples tested in Karnataka was higher than the prescribed limit. 
The companies had reportedly tested samples at 700-800 fuel stations across the country but had not found problems alleged by the state govt, Vijayendra said.
Leader of the opposition, R Ashoka, wondered whether Karnataka had laboratories equipped to conduct high-quality tests and raised doubts over the reliability of the samples being examined.
“Nobody knows where the samples were collected from — govt godowns or petrol bunks. If they were collected from bunks, who can guarantee that additional ethanol was not mixed with the fuel?” he asked.

stories.headline: Rajajinagar murders: Two more bodies recovered near Chamundi hills in Mysuru
stories.deck: With this development, five bodies have been traced so far in the case, while the search for the remaining two continues
stories.bodyText:
In a fresh development in the brutal murder of seven members of a family, Rajajinagar Police have recovered two more bodies, suspected to be those of Shivakumar and his wife Divya — the accused Indushekhar’s brother-in-law and sister-in-law — near the foothills of Chamundi Hills in Mysuru, on Sunday (November 8, 2026).
Police conducted a spot mahazar of the spot with the accused while recovering the bodies.
With this development, five bodies have been traced so far in the case, while the search for the remaining two continues.
DCP, North Division said that two more dead bodies found near Chamundi hill forest area are said to be of Shivakumar and Divya. Another special police team has been deployed to Shiradi Ghat, where it is conducting searches for the two more missing bodies, he said.
On Saturday (November 7, 2026), police recovered the bodies of the accused’s wife, Sunita, and mother-in-law, Rupavathi, from a forest area in Salem, Tamil Nadu. The body of a young boy was earlier recovered near the foothills of Nandi Hills and has already been cremated.
According to the investigation, Indushekhar allegedly murdered seven of his relatives, including his wife, over a period of 15 days. He is suspected to have packed the bodies in gunny bags, transported them in his car and dumped them at different locations, including the foothills of Nandi Hills, a forest area in Salem, the foothills of Chamundi Hills and Shiradi Ghat.
The accused, who is currently in police custody, is being subjected to intensive interrogation as investigators try to establish the sequence of murders, the motive and the locations where the remaining bodies were disposed of.

He directed metro officials to restore roads affected by the construction without delay. “Potholes on connecting roads must be repaired within a week. Roads at lower levels, which are prone to flooding, also need to be improved,” he told officials.

briefs.headline: BJP, Congress functionaries clash over who gets credit for Bengaluru Metro
briefs.bodyText:
Bengaluru: Ahead of the inauguration of Namma Metro’s Pink Line this week, the ruling 
Congress
 and opposition 
BJP
 have once again crossed swords over who deserves credit for the city’s crucial transport project.
On Sunday, Bangalore South MP and BJP leader 
Tejasvi Surya
 claimed that the Union govt had taken Metro connectivity in the city from just 7km in 2014 to over 100km in 2026. He also alleged that Karnataka’s Congress-led govt had perfected the art of delay, hypocrisy and misplaced priorities. “Across all approved phases of Bengaluru Metro — phase 1, 2, 2A & 2B, and 3 — the Union govt has committed Rs 41,557 crore towards construction. Karnataka govt’s committed contribution stands at Rs 36,332 crore,” Surya said.
According to the MoU, Bengaluru Metro follows a funding model which includes contributions from the Centre and state, along with soft loans from international bilateral and multilateral agencies. “These loans are secured directly by BMRCL and carry the sovereign guarantee of the central govt... The state govt cannot inspire confidence to secure such financing on its own because of its ‘khali trunk.’ It is the central govt’s sovereign guarantee that makes these international loans possible,” the MP added.
He also accused the state of presiding over delays, extensions and cost escalations across infrastructure projects, while announcing car-centric projects.
Responding to Surya’s allegations, former health minister and Gandhinagar MLA Dinesh Gundu Rao said the state bears 84% of the Metro project’s cost. “Karnataka bears 84% of the cost of Namma Metro, while the Centre contributes a paltry 16%. You wouldn’t know it from the way BJP talks about it,” he stated on his X account.
He added that while welcoming the Prime Minister for the Pink Line’s opening, credit should be given to Karnataka govt, its people, and the taxpayers for making it all possible.

briefs.headline: I PU question papers to be set at State level in Karnataka
briefs.bodyText:
To improve the quality of Pre-University (PU) education, the Department of School Education has decided to prepare the question papers for the I PU annual examinations at the State level from the current academic year.

stories.headline: Oil falls as Donald Trump says new Iran attacks ‘unlikely’
stories.deck: On November 8, 2026, ​Iraq reached an understanding with the U.S. to allow Iraqi oil exports through the Strait of Hormuz via ⁠a shipping lane near Oman
stories.bodyText:
Oil prices fell at Monday’s (November 9, 2026) open after U.S. President Donald Trump said he was highly unlikely to order new Iran attackswhile talks to end the conflict make progress, despite both nations’ reports of attacks on ships in or near the Strait of Hormuz.
Brent was down 84 cents, or 0.85%, to $97.48 a barrel by 0138 GMT, while West Texas Intermediate fell 32 cents, or 0.35%, to $90.51 a barrel.
The fall reversed minor gains made on Friday’s (November 6, 2026) settlement as the market assessed the possibility of further U.S. strikes on Iran, although Brent fell 17% last week, the steepest weekly drop since the start of the COVID pandemic and the biggest in absolute terms, according to LSEG data dating back to 1988.
“It depends on whether or not they sign a very strong agreement,” Trump told CNN in a phone interview. “The answer is, highly unlikely it’s going to be necessary.”
Mr. Trump had hinted at renewing attacks on Iran after last week’s U.S. midterm elections, but there has been no sign of a large-scale U.S. military operation. Iran has said it would respond by striking U.S. and Israeli targets.
Tim Waterer, chief analyst at KCM Trade, called Mr. Trump’s comments “more measured” but said “the market is still waiting to see whether the midterms have produced a lasting shift in Trump’s approach to the conflict, or whether this is just another temporary change in tone.”
Oil is headed for a glut again as recovering West Asian oil flows, rising production from other countries and weak demand have pushed global supply above consumption, JPMorgan said in a report on Friday (November 6, 2026), estimating a surplus of 1.1 million barrels per day in September, widening to 1.4 million bpd in October.
On Sunday (November 8, 2026), Iraq reached an understanding with the U.S. to allow Iraqi oil exports through the Strait of Hormuz via a shipping lane near Oman, Foreign Minister Fuad Hussein said in an interview with Al Jazeera.
He said Iraq’s losses from the Iran war and disruptions to oil exports had reached $60 billion.
Separately the Houthis claimed responsibility for an attack on Saudi Aramco’s offices in the capital Riyadh on Sunday that left windows blown out but no reported casualties.

stories.headline: Brent crude falls over $1 as Trump signals fresh US strikes on Iran are unlikely
stories.deck: On Monday, oil prices experienced a downturn following Donald Trump's remarks about military options regarding Iran. He suggested that if negotiations were successful, further military action would likely be avoided. Despite this, concerns linger about potential shipping disruptions in the Strait of Hormuz, which continue to threaten global crude supply chains.
stories.bodyText:
Oil prices opened lower on Monday, with Brent crude briefly shedding more than $1 a barrel.
The dip comes after US President Donald Trump said that fresh American strikes on Iran were “highly unlikely” if negotiations between the two countries made progress.
Brent crude futures fell 52 cents, or 0.53%, to $97.80 a barrel. US West Texas Intermediate (WTI) crude futures slipped 15 cents, or 0.17%, to $90.68 a barrel.
Trump's comments offered an indication that the US could avoid another round of military action against Iran, provided Tehran agreed to what he described as a strong deal. However, reports from both countries of shipping being hit in and around the Strait of Hormuz kept concerns over disruptions to the strategic waterway alive.
Trump warns Iran despite ruling out fresh strikes
"It depends on whether or not they sign a very strong agreement," Trump told CNN in a phone interview. "The answer is, highly unlikely it's going to be necessary."
In a 20-minute telephone interview with CNN, Trump repeated five times that renewed military intervention was unlikely if Iran made tangible progress in negotiations over its nuclear programme and the reopening of the Strait of Hormuz.
The US president, however, warned that Washington had identified 38 Iranian bridges that could be destroyed within an hour if further military action became necessary.
"We have 38 bridges in our site that we can knock down in literally one hour. They’ll all be down," Trump told CNN.
Hormuz caught in chokehold
The remarks come amid continued disruption to crude oil supplies through the Strait of Hormuz, which has now lasted for over eight months. The disruption has affected refinery operations across major Asian and Middle Eastern economies.
According to the US Energy Information Administration (EIA), global refinery activity fell sharply in the second quarter of 2026 after the Middle East conflict broke out.
Data from energy intelligence firm Kpler showed that global refinery inputs dropped by 4.8 million barrels per day (b/d), or 6%, in April-June compared with the previous quarter. However, they recovered by 1.8 million b/d in the third quarter as refiners adapted to changing trade flows and alternative supply routes.
Countries that rely heavily on crude supplies passing through the Strait of Hormuz were among the worst affected.
China saw the biggest decline, with refinery inputs falling by 2.1 million b/d in the second quarter and a further 0.8 million b/d in the third quarter.
India, South Korea and Japan together recorded a drop of more than 1 million b/d in crude oil inputs in the second quarter. Their combined inputs recovered by 0.8 million b/d in the following quarter.

stories.headline: India's crypto tax could hurt blockchain innovation: Buterin
stories.bodyText:
MUMBAI: India's cryptocurrency tax regime could hamper blockchain innovation and undermine the country's potential to become a hub for building core blockchain infrastructure, Ethereum co-founder Vitalik Buterin said.
Speaking on the sidelines of Devcon, Ethereum's annual global developer conference, in Mumbai, the 32-year-old Russian-Canadian programmer said the 30% tax on crypto gains and 1% tax deducted at source (TDS) on transfers could disproportionately burden smaller developers and discourage innovation. Buterin pointed to proposals in the US for a de minimis exemption on small-value transactions and tax exemptions in some countries for assets held for over a year. India needed a regulatory framework that allowed developers to experiment without excessive compliance burdens, he suggested.
He believes India can move beyond supplying developers to global technology companies. Its large Ethereum developer community, open-technology culture and govt-backed open-source initiatives offer grounds for optimism, he said.
Buterin, who proposed Ethereum in 2013 at the age of 19, helped expand blockchain's use beyond digital currency. 
The platform, launched in 2015, allows developers to build applications using blockchain technology.
"There is a lot of excitement from people who want to build open technology, both inside Ethereum and outside, and we wanted to engage with that," he said, explaining India's choice as the venue for Devcon. He also sees scope for blockchain to complement India's digital public infrastructure, particularly UPI and govt services.

briefs.headline: Cheaper Scotch raises stakes for desi whisky
briefs.bodyText:
BENGALURU: Cheaper Scotch is putting Indian whisky makers under pressure, even as lower import duties offer savings to companies that use it in their blends. For small distillers that make their own spirits, an imported label can now cost substantially less than a locally made bottle.
Huli's rice malt whisky was launched in Karnataka at Rs 2,650 for 750ml. By comparison, J&B Rare was priced at Rs 1,375 at Bengaluru retailer Tonique in October, according to TOI's earlier reporting. At these prices, J&B Rare cost Rs 1,275 less, or about half as much. Tonique said the price had fallen from Rs 2,835, attributing the reduction to local bottling.
"The smaller players will not be able to survive," said Huli Spirits founder Aruna Urs. Her Mysuru distillery makes spirits from locally sourced paddy and jaggery and does not import Scotch.
Arun Kumar Parasa of Unistil Alcoblends said falling Scotch prices had adversely affected the Indian single malt industry. Lower duties on bulk Scotch imported by some small and medium distilleries would benefit them "very marginally", he said.
The distinction is between making spirits locally and buying imported whisky for bottling or blending. 
Bulk Scotch arrives in large containers and can be bottled here or used as an ingredient in Indian whisky.
A lower import bill can help these manufacturers, while cheaper finished bottles intensify competition for other producers.
Jason Holway, senior consultant at drinks research firm IWSR, expects the price gap to narrow further. "Depending on the state, cheaper blended Scotches are expected to become more attractively priced than they used to be and may not be much more expensive than domestic premium brands using Scotch as an ingredient."
India's trade agreement with Britain cut Scotch import duties from 150% to 75%. Customs officials subsequently questioned whether certain bulk shipments qualified for the lower duty. On Nov 2, commerce secretary Rajesh Agrawal assured manufacturers that the duty benefits would be protected, with commerce and revenue officials to work on resolving the classification dispute.
An industry executive, speaking on condition of anonymity, said Indian buyers were also negotiating better purchase prices from Scotland. The executive estimated that the duty reduction could lower retail prices by roughly 8-10%, depending on state taxes and companies' pricing decisions. Distribution difficulties and advertising restrictions remained longstanding hurdles for small manufacturers, the executive added.
IWSR's figures also show the limits of India's shift towards expensive whisky. Its premium-and-above category, defined as Rs 2,899.01 or more per 750ml bottle, accounted for less than 1% of whisky consumed by volume in 2025, Holway said.

briefs.headline: Distribution ring-fenced from impact of new Irdai norms: LIC
briefs.bodyText:
'IDBI Bank sale not to have significant impact on business'
MUMBAI: LIC has said it is in an advantageous position under Irdai's new distribution norms and it also has taken steps to ring-fence the performance of bancassurance channels despite the impending sale of IDBI Bank - its largest bank distribution partner. Officials cited low expense ratio, diversified distribution network and declining dependence on IDBI Bank.
LIC CEO and managing director R Doraiswamy said the insurer's cost structure gave it an advantage over competitors, even if they reduced distribution costs. "Anybody else reducing the cost of distribution alone will still have to do a lot of work to bring their overall expense ratio to be under that. So, we stand to be on a distinctly advantageous position, and will be closely watching the market as it unfolds," he said in an analysts' call.
On the proposed IDBI Bank stake sale, Hemant Buch, executive director, marketing, bancassurance and alternate channels, said LIC did not expect a significant decline in business sourced through the lender. IDBI Bank's contribution has moderated from historical highs to around 20% of LIC's total bank-driven business and about 30% of its bancassurance volume.
"While IDBI will continue to deliver value for us and remain a valued and esteemed partner, we do not foresee much depletion in terms of their contribution and overall impact on the volume of bancassurance-driven performance," Buch said. 
He added that LIC was expanding its partnerships with other public and private sector lenders. Govt has recently approved sale of LIC and govt stake in IDBI Bank to Fairfax group.
Doraiswamy also said product pricing did not depend solely on the total expenses built into a policy. He said competitors relying more heavily on non-agent distribution channels or lower distribution costs would still need to reduce their overall expense ratios to match LIC's cost structure.
"We would like to protect the interest of our agents in as much as whatever is possible within the regulatory framework, and that is why we have given our specific recommendations on some areas which concern the points raised by the agents' groups as well. We hope that there will be a good discussion, and when the version of draft regulations are released," said Doraiswamy.
"In last couple of years, in fact, dependence on IDBI has, in fact, moderated. What it used to be around 50% to bank-driven business and almost 40% to total bancassurance business of corporation, it has moderated to around 20% of total and 30% to bank. Further moderation also is, in fact, taking place despite the, in fact, using the fact that IDBI continues to grow, but then, in fact, we also continue to grow with direction coming from, in fact, other partners," said Buch.
Irdai's proposed overhaul of insurance distribution, which seeks to sharply cut commissions, tighten expense limits, curb bank-led sales incentives and restrict loan-linked insurance bundling, has triggered resistance from insurers, banks, brokers and agents who fear loss of revenue, jobs and disruption to established distribution models, even as the regulator seeks to curb mis-selling and reduce costs for policyholders.

briefs.headline: For the first time since 2017, Sensex and Nifty end Muhurat trading in the red
briefs.bodyText:
MUMBAI
: For the second time in 10 years, 
sensex
 and 
Nifty
 both closed lower during the special hour-long trading session on Diwali which marked the start of Samvat year 2083, one of the Hindu calendars which is followed by the Gujarati trading community who dominate the city's share market.
In Sunday's low-volatility, low-volume trading session, sensex opened higher at 81,299 points, was up nearly 300 points from its Friday close, touched a high of 81,442 points, and then profit-taking at higher levels pulled it down to below the 81K mark. Finally, it settled at 80,999 points, down 29 points on the day.
The last time sensex had closed in the red during 
Muhurat trading
 was in 2017. Nifty on NSE also followed a similar trajectory and closed 44 points lower at 24,986 points. For Nifty too, it was the first negative close during the Muhurat session since 2017.
The age-old tradition on Dalal Street is that during the Muhurat trading session on Diwali, domestic investors only buy stocks-even if that order is for one stock-and should never sell. So usually during the Muhurat trading session, leading indices close higher, even if with marginal gains. However, there have been exceptions. And, Sunday's session for the start of Samvat year 2083 was one of those rare ones.
The day's lower close for these indices came after a seven-session rally that added over 10% to take each of the indices to multi-month high levels. The day's modest consolidation appears to reflect natural profit-booking following an exceptional week of gains, said Ponmudi R, CEO of Enrich Money. "Rallies of such magnitude rarely sustain their momentum indefinitely without a period of consolidation, and a single symbolic trading hour was unlikely to buck that pattern."
In Sunday's session, while some of the leading large-cap stocks closed lower, pulling the leading indices lower, midcap and smallcap stocks witnessed buying. As a result, BSE's midcap index closed 0.5% higher while the smallcap index closed 1.5% higher. In turn, the aggregate market capitalisation of all the companies listed on BSE jumped by about Rs 2.6 lakh crore with the current figure at an all-time high of Rs 506 lakh crore, exchange data showed.
The day saw, going by decades-old tradition, families of brokers, traders and other market players going to the exchanges, participating in Lakshmi Puja at the bourse, and some even putting in symbolic trades.
Electronic receipts for silver, platinum soon?
Ashishkumar Chauhan, MD, NSE, said the bourse launched trading in electronic gold receipts (EGRs) on Friday, the day of Dhanteras, traditionally an occasion for buying gold, silver. On the first day itself, over 1.8 lakh EGRs were traded. Chauhan said that in future, similar products could be launched.

briefs.headline: Samvat 2083: What's the outlook for Sensex, Nifty & what should investors do?
briefs.deck: Samvat 2083 outlook: The volatile Muhurat trading session comes after a record seven-day rally by the indices which saw BSE Sensex and Nifty50 rise over 10%. The gains over the preceding seven consecutive sessions had lifted the Sensex by 7,781.99 points, or 10.62%, and the Nifty by 2,331.5 points, or 10.27%.
briefs.bodyText:
Samvat 2083, the beginning of the new accounting year, has started with 
BSE Sensex
 and 
Nifty50
 ending marginally in red.The declines meant that both the Sensex and Nifty ended their eight-year streak of gains during Diwali trading sessions, a run that had continued since 2018.
But investors' wealth surged by Rs 2.60 lakh crore to Rs 5,06,87,267.96 crore. The Nifty-50 declined 0.18 per cent to close at 24,986.40, slipping just below the psychological 25,000 mark after opening higher at 25,070 and touching an intraday high of 25,132.
Muhurat trading
 is a special symbolic session conducted on Diwali, which also marks the beginning of the new Hindu calendar year. The tradition is rooted in the belief that trading during the 'Muhurat', or auspicious period, brings prosperity and financial gains to market participants.
The volatile Muhurat trading session comes after a record seven-day rally by the indices which saw BSE Sensex and Nifty50 rise over 10%. The gains over the preceding seven consecutive sessions had lifted the Sensex by 7,781.99 points, or 10.62%, and the Nifty by 2,331.5 points, or 10.27%.
But Samvat 2082 was a year of negative returns. While BSE Sensex ended 2082, down over 4% from last year’s Muhurat trading, Nifty50 ended with over 3% decline.
According to Motilal Oswal, India stands at a point where a resilient domestic economy meets a challenging external backdrop. Samvat 2082 tested investors’ patience and Samvat 2083 begins on a cautious note, as an external energy shock overshadows a resilient economy.
Will the new year bring cheer for investors? What are the sectors that they should be focusing on? Let’s take a look:
Samvat 2082: The macro-shock year
With negative returns, Samvat 2082 saw several global shocks that took a toll on the stock markets.
Indian markets were affected by several global and domestic factors. Geopolitical tensions in West Asia, elevated crude oil prices, uncertainty around US trade policies and persistent FII selling impacted investor sentiment.
According to Somil Mehta, Head of Retail Research at Mirae Asset Sharekhan, concerns around artificial intelligence also led to selling in IT stocks. Slower earnings growth and expensive valuations in some market segments added to the pressure, he tells TOI.
Neeraj Gaurh, Director & Fund Manager, Anand Rathi AMC sees Samvat 2082 as a year of macro-shocks and not an earnings-shock.
The US-Israel-Iran conflict pushed crude above $110, global bond yields rose and the rupee weakened sharply. That triggered record FPI selling of about Rs 3 lakh crore and a 25 bps RBI hike to 5.50%.
“Domestic money absorbed most of it, with SIPs at a record Rs 32,490 crore. Growth held at 7.8% in Q1 FY27 and bank credit stayed near 18%, so the indices fell on cost of capital and de-rating, not on earnings,” he explains.
Motilal Oswal in a report notes that action also remains in the primary market:
“Jio Platforms’ record IPO and NSE’s listing headlined a busy year, with over 225 companies in the pipeline. Key monitorables include the RBI’s rate trajectory, crude prices, FII flows, trade agreements and earnings growth,” it says.
What’s the outlook for Samvat 2083?
Experts are positive about Samvat 2083 and the recent stock market rally has added to their optimism.
Somil Mehta tells TOI, “We are positive on Indian equities in Samvat 2083 and expect markets to recover gradually. Improving corporate earnings, strong domestic consumption, infrastructure spending and India's long-term growth potential should support market performance.”
“A recovery in foreign investor flows could provide further momentum,” he adds.
Neeraj Gaurh sees Samvat 2083 to be earnings-led, not multiple-led. With nominal GDP at 10–10.5%, FY27 earnings growth of 13%–15% and credit growth near 18%, he expects index returns in the low teens.
“There’s an upside kicker if crude holds below $85–90, the rupee stabilises and global yields ease,” he tells TOI.
Motilal Oswal perceives FY27 to mark a return to double-digit earnings growth, with Nifty EPS expected to grow 16%/14% YoY in FY27/FY28 vs 5% in FY26.
What should investors do?
According to Mehta, investors should use market corrections to accumulate quality companies with strong fundamentals and reasonable valuations.
“A staggered investment approach and diversification across sectors can help create long-term wealth,” he says.
Neeraj Gaurh believes that investors should stay with large caps and select midcaps, keep small caps light, favour private banks, manufacturing/capex and discretionary consumption, stay selective in IT and real estate, and deploy in stages rather than chase the recent rally.
“I’d revisit if crude holds above $90, developed-market yields rise further, or RBI tightening runs past 50–75 bps,” he adds.
Over the last 10 completed Samvat years (2072–2081), the Nifty delivered a compounded annual return of approximately 12.6%, while the Sensex delivered around 12.5%. The Nifty generated positive returns in nine out of these ten years.
Somil Mehta points out that this highlights the long-term wealth creation potential of Indian equities despite periodic corrections and volatility.
Motilal Oswal says that Nifty valuations are attractive at 17.5x forward earnings, 16% below the long-term average.
“After a nearly 10% correction from record highs, midcaps trade 6% below their long-term average, while smallcaps remain at a 25% premium; thus one needs to follow a selective approach in stock picking,” the brokerage says.

briefs.headline: Samsung set to become South Korea's first company with 200 trillion won in cash
briefs.deck: Samsung Electronics is on the cusp of exceeding 200 trillion won in cash assets, driven by the soaring AI semiconductor market. Over the past year, the company has dramatically bolstered its cash reserves, nearly doubling their value. With a commitment to semiconductor infrastructure and a strong shareholder return scheme, Samsung is solidifying its financial position.
briefs.bodyText:
Samsung Electronics is on course to become the first company in South Korea to build cash assets of more than 200 trillion won ($146.6 billion), with the artificial intelligence (AI)-driven semiconductor boom strengthening its financial position.
The chipmaker's cash reserves have nearly doubled over the past year, while its overall assets have also grown. The increase comes as Samsung prepares for higher investments in semiconductor manufacturing and research, alongside a sizeable shareholder return programme.
Samsung's cash and cash equivalents are estimated to have reached 214.8 trillion won by the end of the third quarter, according to industry data released on Sunday. This marks a rise of 24.8 trillion won from the 190 trillion won recorded at the end of the previous quarter, as reported by Yonhap news agency.
The latest estimate is also almost twice the 108.5 trillion won the company held at the end of the third quarter of 2025.
Samsung's total assets stood at 791.8 trillion won at the end of September, an increase of 32.4 trillion won over the preceding three months.
The company's growing cash position is expected to be enough to cover the highest possible payout under its landmark shareholder return policy announced in August, market watchers estimate.
Samsung had indicated that it would make between 90 trillion won and 110 trillion won available for shareholder returns in 2026.
The company is also expected to announce its shareholder policy for the coming year at a board meeting scheduled for January.
Alongside shareholder payouts, Samsung is preparing for a significant increase in spending on its semiconductor business.
Investments in chipmaking infrastructure and research and development are expected to exceed 100 trillion won this year, marking a historic high. Of this amount, 84.4 trillion won is expected to go towards expanding its memory production facilities.
Samsung expects the semiconductor supercycle to extend through next year, supported by continued investments in artificial intelligence and a crunch in memory supply.

briefs.headline: Indian Oil plans to buy its own oil, LPG ships as freight costs surge 4 times
briefs.deck: To bolster its shipping logistics, Indian Oil Corporation is planning to acquire its own carriers and is looking into shipbuilding ventures within India as part of the Make in India initiative. The rise in geopolitical tensions has led to higher shipping costs, necessitating these strategic changes. IOC has also diversified its crude sourcing to minimize supply disruptions and leverage market…
briefs.bodyText:
With shipping costs rising sharply and movement around the Strait of Hormuz facing disruptions, 
Indian Oil Corporation
 (IOC) is looking to take greater control of how its crude oil and liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) reach its refineries.
The state-owned oil major plans to purchase its own carriers and is also exploring the possibility of getting ships built in India.
IOC's board has approved the purchase of a few vessels, and tenders for the proposed acquisitions were issued several months ago, director of finance Anuj Jain said during the company's second-quarter earnings call.
"The country needs oil sector companies to focus more on the shipping area now," Jain said, adding that the company was examining shipbuilding opportunities in India under the government's Make in India initiative.
The proposed purchases could change the way IOC manages its shipping requirements. The company has traditionally depended on time-chartered and voyage-chartered vessels but is now looking at a combination of owning ships, improving existing charter arrangements and encouraging domestic shipbuilding.
Shipping costs jump as Hormuz disruptions tighten the squeeze
The rising cost of transporting crude oil and LPG has made shipping arrangements an important part of IOC's strategy. 
Geopolitical tensions in the Middle East have disrupted commercial movement near the Strait of Hormuz, leading to higher freight rates and war-risk insurance costs.
IOC currently has three crude oil carriers and nine LPG vessels under time-charter arrangements. These have helped it contain transportation expenses during the current crisis, Jain said.
The difference between chartered and spot-market rates has been particularly sharp. IOC pays around $2-2.50 per barrel for its time-chartered crude carriers, against spot-market rates of up to $8-10 per barrel.
The pressure is even more pronounced in LPG transportation. Freight rates that would generally be around $40 per tonne have climbed to $160-180 per tonne in the spot market, Jain said.
Russia accounts for 55% of IOC's crude sourcing
Alongside its plans to strengthen shipping capacity, IOC has changed the geographical mix of its crude purchases to diversify supplies and limit exposure to disruptions.
Russia supplied 55 per cent of the company's crude requirements in the first half of the current financial year. Middle Eastern countries accounted for another 24 per cent, while Africa contributed around 10 per cent.
Brazil supplied 7 per cent of IOC's crude, the United States accounted for 2-5 per cent and Venezuela contributed 3-4 per cent, Jain said.
The company has also moved towards greater reliance on spot purchases. These accounted for around 87 per cent of its crude sourcing in the first half of FY27, against approximately 50 per cent in the previous financial year.
IOC has managed to negotiate discounts against benchmark prices despite fluctuations in the global market. The premium or discount paid over benchmark crude during the September quarter ranged from a discount of $5 per barrel to a premium of $12 per barrel. In the preceding quarter, the range was between zero and a premium of $18 per barrel.
Jain said IOC continued to purchase Russian crude at what it described as optimal prices and was also processing Venezuelan crude.
Crude prices climb to around $120 per barrel in October
The company's procurement strategy comes amid a sharp rise in oil prices following the escalation of US-Iran hostilities towards the end of February.
Indian basket crude, which averaged around $65-70 per barrel in February, stayed above $100 for much of the first quarter. It averaged approximately $120 per barrel in October, Jain said.
Despite the supply-chain challenges, IOC has kept its refinery operations at optimal levels while building up inventories to provide a buffer against disruptions.
Its crude oil inventory has increased to around 39 days from the usual 33-35 days. The company was also holding 20 days of LPG inventory and 23-25 days of petrol and diesel stocks.
Inventory gains help IOC report Rs 21,630 crore profit
IOC's net profit rose to Rs 21,630 crore in the September quarter, compared with a loss of Rs 2,661 crore in the preceding quarter. The company had reported a profit of Rs 7,610 crore in the corresponding period last year.
Inventory gains and improved performance across several businesses contributed to the quarterly profitability, the company said.
IOC recorded a gross refining margin of $18.52 per barrel, excluding the impact of the special additional excise duty. Its inventory gain stood at Rs 6,948 crore during the quarter.
However, the company continues to face uncertainty from geopolitical developments. Jain said these remained a key concern, particularly because of their impact on crude procurement, freight costs and marketing margins.
IOC's plans to acquire vessels and explore shipbuilding in India come as it looks to strengthen its control over transportation alongside diversifying its crude purchases.

briefs.headline: Adani Enterprises plans ₹35,000-40,000 crore annual capex in next two years
briefs.deck: The planned spending comes as the group seeks to scale up businesses built over recent years, including airports and data centres, while bringing its large manufacturing investments closer to commercial operation.
briefs.bodyText:
Adani Enterprises Ltd. plans to spend between ₹35,000 crore and ₹40,000 crore annually over the next couple of years, with airports, data centres and its proposed PVC complex emerging as the biggest investment drivers as the conglomerate steps up expansion across its infrastructure businesses.
"We expect to do capex at a run rate of around ₹40,000 crore. So, we may be somewhere in the range of Rs 35,000 crore to Rs 40,000 crore, which is the rate we expect to continue over the next couple of years," Manan Vakharia, head of finance at Adani Enterprises, said during the company's earnings call.
The planned spending comes as the group seeks to scale up businesses built over recent years, including airports and data centres, while bringing its large manufacturing investments closer to commercial operation.
"The heavy lifting will be done by airports, data centres and PVC," Mr. Vakharia said.
Adani Enterprises, the flagship incubator of the Adani Group, reported its highest-ever half-year EBITDA of ₹11,958 crore for the six months ended September 2026, an increase of 56% from a year earlier.
Consolidated income rose 62% to Rs 71,569 crore, while profit before tax from continuing operations increased 45 per cent to Rs 3,297 crore.
Chief Executive Officer Arun Bansal said the company was progressively moving from a "build-out phase to value realisation phase", as investments made over the past few years begin contributing more meaningfully to earnings.
The airport business and data centres are central to that transition. Adani Airport Holdings reported a 52% increase in first-half EBITDA to ₹3,275 crore, while AdaniConneX, its data-centre joint venture, has expanded its contracted capacity to more than 1.2 gigawatts.
AdaniConneX signed a new 240-megawatt hyperscale contract during the September quarter. Its operational capacity stood at 94.6 MW after handing over an additional 29.2 MW to customers during the period.
The company expects operational capacity to reach 120-150 MW by the end of the current financial year and approach 500 MW over the following 12-18 months, when the facilities are expected to begin generating billing revenue.
Of the 1.4 GW of data-centre capacity being developed, 1.2 GW has already been tied up and is at different stages of implementation and construction, its management said.
The airport portfolio, which comprises eight airports, including Navi Mumbai International Airport, accounts for about 23% of India's passenger traffic and 29% of its air cargo volumes, according to the company officials.
Adani Airport Holdings handled 21.3 million passengers in the September quarter. Its revenue rose 20% year-on-year to ₹3,786 crore, while EBITDA increased 55% to ₹1,641 crore. Non-aeronautical revenue grew 57%, significantly faster than the 9% increase in aeronautical revenue.
Navi Mumbai International Airport began international operations on July 15.
The Management expects the airport to reach its full annual capacity of 20 million passengers by the end of FY28, supported by the expansion of domestic and international routes and the transfer of some international flights from existing Mumbai airports.
The company's other major investment is a 1-million-tonne-per-annum PVC manufacturing complex at Mundra, Gujarat, involving capital expenditure of about ₹26,000 crore.
Around 60% of the project spending and construction has been completed, and the first part of the complex is expected to be commissioned in the next financial year. The facility will also include related chemicals and chlor-alkali operations.
Separately, Adani Enterprises has completed the expansion of its solar module manufacturing capacity to 10 GW and expects to commission 6 GW of solar cell capacity by the end of the current financial year. The company sold 1,478 MW of solar modules in the September quarter, up 35% from a year earlier.
The proposed investment cycle will require the company to balance expansion with project execution and the generation of returns from newly commissioned assets.
Management did not provide a specific EBITDA forecast for FY27. PTI ANZ BAL
