stories.headline: As Magnus Carlsen and 23 others await, Total Chess chief defends fast classical stage
stories.deck: Total Chess chief Kjell Madland has defended the pilot tournament’s fast classical-only group stage, insisting all 24 players will compete across formats until the final day. The Budapest event opens with a nine-round blitz tournament, followed by a fast classical group stage that decides the four semi-finalists, with all three formats used in the knockouts. Madland said the format aims to…
stories.bodyText:
NEW DELHI: World No. 1 
Magnus Carlsen
 and 23 other players are set to take over the board at the Total Chess World Championship Tour pilot in Budapest, but the build-up to the event has been shadowed by questions about its format.
Speaking exclusively to TimesofIndia.com, Total Chess World Championship chief Kjell Madland defended the pilot’s format, under which qualification for the semi-finals is decided purely by fast classical. Rapid and Blitz come into play only after the group stage, which means 20 of the 24 players will not play either format before they are out of the race for the title.
The tournament begins on November 10 at the Anantara New York Palace in Budapest, Hungary. A nine-round Swiss-system blitz tournament and the opening ceremony are held on the same day.
Next up, the 24 players are then split into four groups of six, with the four highest-rated players in separate groups. Each group plays a double round robin at fast classical, which gives 45 minutes per player and a 30-second increment from move one, with three points for a win and one for a draw.
The four group winners go through to the semi-finals, where they play Rapid and Blitz as well as fast classical. 
The other 20 players will play for positions 5 to 24 in all three formats, but they will not be in the race for the finale, which will take place on November 20.
Madland, the founder and CEO of Norway Chess and the Total Chess World Championship Tour, rejected the suggestion that those 20 players are sidelined.
“They are not eliminated,” he told this website. “All the players will play all the games until the last day.”
The nine-round Blitz Swiss does not count towards qualification, but its standings break ties in the group tables. “If players are tied in the group stage, then we will look at the results in the blitz tournament to decide who is number two, three and four,” Madland added.
He said the group stage uses fast classical because the time control, announced by FIDE in September 2025, is relatively new, and this is the best way to test it.
“Since fast classical is a new format, it’s also good to have attention on this, so we think this is a good way to do it,” he said. “After that, the number one in all the groups will fight for first place, the number two will fight for the next place, and so on. But all the players will play all the games.”
The knockouts use a different structure. The semi-finals, the third-place match and the final are each played over two days. Every day has four Blitz games, then two Rapid games, then one fast classical game, and scores reset each day. If the two days are split or both level, an Armageddon game decides the match. White gets ten minutes with no increment, and Black gets seven minutes with a one-second increment from move 41. A draw, in this case, wins the match for Black.
Madland accepted that the format will draw questions. “Of course, we need to find a good way to do it. This is what we have done, and the players like it,” he noted. “Hopefully it will be good, but there will always be some questions about this and that. Hopefully this will work well.”
He said the pilot status leaves room to adjust, though not drastically.
“We don’t think we will do big adjustments. Hopefully we don’t need to think about that,” he said. “But when we have the pilot, it’s of course much easier if something is needed with rules and regulations. That’s possible. This is of course the reason we have this pilot, to test everything.”
The pilot is the opening event of the Total Chess World Championship Tour 2026–27, which offers two places in the 2028 Candidates Tournament. It was announced by Norway Chess in October 2025, is endorsed by FIDE, and is co-organised with the Hungarian Chess Federation.
Madland said the response so far has been positive.
“We have received a lot of good feedback from everywhere, from players, from media and from fans,” he said. “People are very open to this, and I feel that people have also waited for something like this, because combining all the formats is a way to find the best players.”
On why the format was built this way, he said: “I had a feeling for some years that we should build something that included everything, because we have talked with players, fans, media and everything.” He added that it would help the sport grow “in the media, in OTT and TV channels, in media deals.”
“I hope people find this very interesting, and also that they are open to seeing that chess needs to change a bit to meet the new audience, so there will be more interest in it,” he said.

stories.headline: Marnus Labuschagne dropped! Australia chief selector makes big announcement
stories.deck: Marnus Labuschagne has been excluded from Australia's upcoming Test series against New Zealand following a series of disappointing performances. Chief selector George Bailey highlighted Labuschagne's challenges, noting his lengthy dry spell without a century in 49 innings. The selection for the initial Test will follow the Sheffield Shield matches, but Labuschagne's international journey still…
stories.bodyText:
Marnus Labuschagne
 is set to miss Australia's upcoming Test series against New Zealand, with chief selector 
George Bailey
 confirming that the out-of-form batter will not be considered for the opening Test in December. The decision comes after a prolonged lean patch that has continued through Australia's recent assignments against Bangladesh and South Africa.
Although Australia are yet to announce their squad for the first Test, Bailey made it clear that Labuschagne is currently not in their plans for the New Zealand series, which will be played across December and January.
"At this stage, we won't be considering Marn for selection for certainly that first Test, but for the New Zealand series," Bailey told reporters on Monday.
With speculation mounting over the 31-year-old's position in the side, the selection chair said the decision would also give the batter some clarity as he looks to regain form in domestic cricket.
"There's been a lot of speculation around his place in the team, and so I think this gives him a little bit of space and clears up a bit of conjecture as we work through the next round of [Sheffield] Shield cricket," Bailey added.
This is the second time in the last 17 months that Labuschagne has lost his place in Australia's Test plans. Once a regular fixture at No. 3, he has struggled to produce a century, going 49 innings without one since his last Test hundred during the 2023 Ashes in Manchester.
His previous dip in form had also cost him his place during Australia's tour of the West Indies following last year's World Test Championship final, although he remained part of the squad.
Labuschagne subsequently worked his way back into the playing XI after making a strong start to the domestic season. He returned to his preferred No. 3 position for the home Ashes and began with half-centuries in each of the first two Tests. However, his form faded thereafter, and he has not managed a fifty in his last 16 innings.
His struggles were particularly evident in the recent assignments against Bangladesh and South Africa. Labuschagne managed just 36 runs at an average of 12 against Bangladesh before scoring 131 runs at 21.83 in South Africa. Australia failed to win either series, drawing 1-1 against Bangladesh before suffering a 2-1 defeat in South Africa.
Bailey keeps door open for Labuschagne's return
Despite confirming that Labuschagne would not be considered for the New Zealand series at this stage, Bailey insisted that the batter's international career was far from over.
Australia have a demanding Test schedule ahead, with a five-match tour of India following the four Tests against New Zealand. They are also scheduled to play an away Ashes series next year, leaving Labuschagne with opportunities to force his way back into contention.
"It's still possible, absolutely," Bailey said.
"I think we all know how good and how effective Marnus can be at his best. But that performance hasn't been there. I think he's missed some opportunities, some promising starts in Darwin [against Bangladesh] and even in South Africa as well, to go on and get a big score that we'd like and would have liked for some time, and that just hasn't happened."
Bailey also stressed that Australia had not permanently shut the door on the batter.
"But I don't think we've ever ruled anyone out permanently…and that's no different in this case," he said.
Australia's squad for the opening Test against New Zealand will be announced after the next round of Sheffield Shield matches, which gets underway on Wednesday, November 11.

stories.headline: Olympic boxing champion Imane Khelif set for Paris return
stories.deck: Promoters said this week that Imane Khelif’s December 15 professional fight at the Maison de la Mutualite in Paris will be against undefeated fighter Clarida Sarabia
stories.bodyText:
Olympic boxing champion Imane Khelif is scheduled to return to the ring next month in Paris, two years after she clinched the gold medal in the French capital amid international scrutiny.
Khelif was initially set to fight in April but her bout was postponed after she injured her left shoulder while training.
Promoters said this week that her December 15 professional fight at the Maison de la Mutualite in Paris will be against undefeated fighter Clarida Sarabia.
“I've waited, I've doubted, but deep inside, the fire never dies,” Khelif said on Instagram in a promotional video. “And, now, I'm back.”
Khelif won the Olympic gold at the 2024 Paris Games and was in the spotlight alongside Taiwan's Lin Yu-ting — another gold medal winner — as they faced intense scrutiny fueled by misconceptions about both boxers' sex.
Both fighters were allowed to compete by the IOC after being disqualified from the 2023 world championships by the Russian-dominated International Boxing Association. The IBA claimed the women failed unspecified eligibility tests.
However, the IOC applied sex eligibility rules used in previous Olympics and said Khelif and Lin passed.
World Boxing took over as the sport's governing body last year, and it implemented a sex eligibility policy requiring all fighters to take a one-time genetic test designed to identify the presence of a Y chromosome. Khelif has not competed in World Boxing-sanctioned events since the implementation of the test.

briefs.headline: Arshdeep, Gurnoor Brar, Auqib Nabi to stay back for India’s Test preparations
briefs.deck: India has decided to retain pacers Arshdeep Singh, Gurnoor Brar, and Auqib Nabi for Test preparations. Batting coach Sitanshu Kotak stated that the ODI series conditions have been beneficial for the upcoming Test matches. A preparatory camp for Test players is scheduled to begin on November 11, which will help them get ready. Meanwhile, India leads the ODI series against New Zealand 2-0 after a…
briefs.bodyText:
India pacers 
Arshdeep Singh
, Gurnoor Brar and Auqib Nabi will remain with the team for preparations ahead of the Test series against New Zealand, batting coach Sitanshu Kotak confirmed on Saturday.
The three pacers will stay back after the ODI series as the team begins its preparations for the red-ball challenge.
Speaking at the press conference ahead of the third ODI, Kotak said the conditions in the ongoing ODI series had provided useful preparation for the Test matches, particularly for the bowling unit.
"Both pitches had seam and swing. Good preparations for the Test because the ball will change, but one-day cricket does give you an idea about the conditions. The thickness of the grass and everything. It's been challenging but good for the team and preparations," Kotak said.
He also pointed to the three India A matches as an important part of the build-up, saying they had ensured adequate preparation for both batters and bowlers.
India's Test players are scheduled to begin a preparatory camp on November 11. Kotak expects the sessions to help the squad get ready for the series.
"India Test players will start their camp from the 11th, so hopefully those five-six sessions will help get prepared for the Test series," he said.
Providing details of the team's immediate plans, Kotak confirmed that head coach Gautam Gambhir would remain with the ODI squad, while he and bowling coach 
Morne Morkel
 would travel to Wellington.
"Gurnoor, Arshdeep and Nabi will stay back for Test preparations. Gambhir stays back with the ODI team, me and Morne will go to Wellington. That's the plan for now," he said.
'KL Rahul has played unbelievable innings'
Kotak also spoke about KL Rahul's importance to the Indian batting line-up, praising his adaptability and ability to deliver according to the team's requirements.
Rahul remained unbeaten on 26 during India's rain-affected chase of 135 in the second ODI. With wickets falling at regular intervals, the wicketkeeper-batter held one end together as India reached 113/7 in 26 overs before rain brought the contest to an end.
"Biggest advantage is he opens in Test cricket. He is someone who plays according to the need of the team. Since I have joined, he has played unbelievable innings. Never looks under pressure and has never let the team down. Can rotate and can easily hit sixes," Kotak said.
On India's approach to playing additional all-rounders, the batting coach said team selection was based on players performing their designated roles rather than making compromises to accommodate an extra batter.
"We are playing players at the spot. Difficult to reduce a bowler and add a batter," he explained.
India take 2-0 series lead
Meanwhile, India moved 2-0 ahead in the five-match ODI series after edging New Zealand by four runs under the DLS method in Wellington.
Defending a modest target of 135 in a contest reduced to 47 overs per side, New Zealand had India in trouble at 113/7 after 26 overs when rain forced the players off the field. India were four runs ahead of the DLS par score, handing them victory.
Gurnoor Brar was the standout performer with the ball, claiming 4/30 in 10 overs, while Auqib Nabi picked up two wickets. Anshul Kamboj and Axar Patel also finished with two wickets apiece.
Earlier, Daryl Mitchell top-scored for New Zealand with 55, rescuing the hosts from 53/5 through a 59-run partnership with Mitchell Santner, who contributed 31.
India will now head to Hamilton for the third ODI on Tuesday, looking to extend their advantage in the series.

briefs.headline: Chennai Open tennis: Singles final postponed due to rain, unhealthy air quality
briefs.deck: The final will now be held at 11 a.m. on November 9; spectators with valid tickets for the postponed game will be allowed to enter the venue with the same tickets
briefs.bodyText:
The singles final of the WTA 250 Chennai Open between Indonesia’s Janice Tjen and Poland’s Magda Linette was postponed due to rain and poor air quality on Sunday.
The contest will now be held at 11 a.m. on Monday, the reserve day for the tournament.
The summit clash was to take place after the doubles final and scheduled for a 6:30 p.m. start on Sunday. While the doubles fixture finished without any interruption, the singles final was delayed thrice due to rain. The precipitation finally relented for good, allowing the organisers to dry the centre court at the SDAT Stadium in Nungambakkam and announce that the contest would get underway at 9 p.m. However, an hour after that update, the play was called off due to the smog caused by Deepavali firecrackers creating visibility issues. Accuweather described the air quality as “unhealthy” at that time.
Both players came to the centre court and had a brief discussion with supervisor Sheetal Iyer before taking their kit bags and leaving again.
Later, in an official statement, WTA said, “Due to unforeseen weather conditions, the Women’s Singles Final between Janice Tjen and Magda Linette has been postponed. The match will now take place tomorrow (November 9, 2026) at 11 a.m.”
Tamil Nadu Tennis Association has announced that the spectators with valid tickets for Sunday’s play will be allowed to enter the venue on Monday with the same tickets.
The third edition of the WTA 250 event had begun with a complete washout on the opening day of the main draw action. Rain had interrupted play for an hour on the second day as well.
For the foreseeable future, this is the last Tour-level event on Indian soil. The tournament has been reallocated to Manila, the Philippines, for 2027 due to the growing popularity of Filipino star Alexandra Eala as well as the current time slot being unsuitable for Chennai due to the monsoon season.

briefs.headline: WTA Chennai Open: Vaishnavi and Rutuja settle for runners-up finish against Swiss duo
briefs.deck: Vaishnavi, 21, and Rutuja, 30, had already created history by becoming the first-ever all-Indian pair to reach the final of a WTA Tour event
briefs.bodyText:
The dream run of Vaishnavi Adkar and Rutuja Bhosale ended in a runner-up finish at the WTA 250 Chennai Open on Sunday (November 8, 2026) as the home favourites went down 2-6, 0-6 to the Swiss duo of Simona Waltert and Naima Karamoko in the final.
Vaishnavi, 21, and Rutuja, 30, had already created history by becoming the first-ever all-Indian pair to reach the final of a WTA Tour event. They were looking to join former World No. 1 Sania Mirza and Ankita Raina on the list of Indian titlists at this level.
However, in the summit clash which lasted an hour and 10 minutes, they fell well short of causing any trouble for Waltert and Karamoko in front of 700-odd spectators on centre court at the SDAT Stadium in Nungambakkam here.
The Swiss pair got off the blocks quickly and raced to a 4-0 lead in the opener, breaking both the Indians’ serves with ease.
World No. 128 Rutuja and World No. 359 Vaishnavi got one break back as Waltert overcooked a backhand down the line on deciding point in the fifth game. But despite the late resurgence of the home pair, the Swiss duo maintained its slender advantage before breaking Vaishnavi’s serve again to clinch the first set.
Former Doubles World No. 1 Rohan Bopanna, who is Vaishnavi’s mentor and had won the mixed doubles gold with Rutuja at the Hangzhou Asian Games, came down from the stands to the players’ box to encourage the two though the second essay turned out to be completely one-sided. World No. 99 Karamoka showed why she was the best doubles player on the court with her impressive poaching skills on multiple occasions while Waltert, predominantly a singles player, kept things solid from the baseline.
Karamoko won her maiden Tour-level title while for Waltert, it was her second after the triumph in Lausanne in 2021 with compatriot Susan Bandecchi.
“We played together for the first time and won the title, so it couldn’t be better. I really hope we can play some more weeks together and we’ll try to enjoy this one as long as possible,” said the 29-year-old Karamoko.
“It’s amazing to win a title and to actually finish the last tournament of the season like this. We played at a great level throughout the week. We got used to each other a bit more and yes, it was a really fun game to spend the week together and I’m looking forward to many more matches with Naima,” added Waltert.
The doubles final began at 4 p.m. but the Deepavali fireworks had already started. Playing in such an atmosphere was a challenge for the Swiss duo. “Actually, we have never played in such a situation. You can still hear them (the fireworks) now. It was a bit disturbing at the beginning of the week and now, we almost don’t hear them anymore,” said Karamoko.
“They (the organisers) also told us that it’s going to be the worst today (in terms of fireworks). So, we were also prepared and that’s how we adapted and dealt with it,” added the 25-year-old Waltert.
Champions Karamoko and Waltert received USD 13,600 while runners-up Vaishnavi and Rutuja earned USD 7,650 in prize money. Aadhav Arjuna, Tamil Nadu’s Minister for Public Works and Sports Development, presented the two pairs with their respective trophies.

briefs.headline: P.T. Usha complains to IOA electoral officer over WhatsApp campaign for SOM polls
briefs.deck: The Indian Olympic Association president alleged former archer Dola Banerjee violated the Model Code of Conduct by circulating a WhatsApp message seeking votes for four candidates ahead of Monday’s election
briefs.bodyText:
Indian Olympic Association (IOA) president P.T. Usha has lodged a complaint with the Electoral Officer alleging that former archer Dola Banerjee violated the Model Code of Conduct by circulating a WhatsApp message soliciting votes for a panel of four candidates in Monday’s (November 9, 2026) Sportspersons of Outstanding Merit (SOM) elections.
In her complaint, Usha objected to a WhatsApp message circulated through an account bearing Banerjee’s name, seeking support for the ‘New Bharat Panel’ and asking voters to elect four named candidates, along with their ballot serial numbers and roll numbers.
Usha cited Clause 1.9 of the Model Code of Conduct, issued on October 30, 2026, which states that the promotion of a candidate shall exclude any form of publicity, including the use of new media or social networks. She contended that the circulation of the message amounted to targeted solicitation of votes through social media, and appeared to fall within the ambit of the clause. The complaint also referred to Clauses 1.2 and 1.3, which require candidates to conduct their campaigns fairly, with dignity and moderation, and to show due respect to other candidates.
Usha has urged the election authorities to examine the communication, establish the circumstances under which it was created and circulated, and seek an explanation from the persons concerned. She has also sought appropriate action under the applicable election rules if a violation is established, along with directions to ensure a level playing field for all candidates.
With polling scheduled from 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. on November 9, 2026, Usha has sought urgent intervention and a decision before voting begins. A screenshot of the WhatsApp message and a copy of the Model Code of Conduct were enclosed with the complaint.

briefs.headline: Antonelli crowned champion! Verstappen, Hamilton, Russell and Leclerc battle for P2
briefs.deck: Kimi Antonelli has clinched the 2026 Drivers' Championship, sparking a fierce battle for P2 among Max Verstappen, Lewis Hamilton, George Russell, and Charles Leclerc. Due to grid penalties, these top drivers will begin from outside the top six, making their pursuit for points more challenging. The Sao Paulo Grand Prix at Interlagos is notorious for its erratic weather conditions, ensuring every…
briefs.bodyText:
Kimi Antonelli has conquered Formula 1, but the fight for the next biggest prize is far from over. With the 2026 Drivers' Championship already decided, the spotlight shifts to an intriguing four-way battle for second place as Formula 1 arrives at Interlagos for Sunday's Sao Paulo Grand Prix.
Just 16 points separate Max Verstappen, Lewis Hamilton, George Russell and Charles Leclerc, with four races remaining in the season. Verstappen holds the advantage, but Hamilton is breathing down his neck, while Russell and Leclerc remain firmly within striking distance. And with Interlagos known for unpredictable weather, dramatic overtakes and late-race twists, the battle for P2 could take another fascinating turn in Brazil.
But there is an added twist: all four contenders will start outside the top six after a series of grid penalties. Verstappen and Hamilton will start from the back of the grid, while Leclerc and Russell have also been pushed down the order. What could have been a straightforward fight for championship points has now turned into a major recovery challenge.
F1 Drivers' Championship standings: Who leads the battle for P2?
With Antonelli already crowned world champion after securing the title at the Mexico City Grand Prix, the remaining focus is on who will finish behind the Italian.
Here is how the four contenders stand heading into the Sao Paulo GP:
Verstappen leads Hamilton by just two points, while Russell is 11 behind the Dutchman and Leclerc trails by 16. With 100 points still available across the final four rounds before Sunday's race, none of the four can afford a poor weekend.
The battle is particularly interesting because Verstappen and Russell have three victories each this season, while Hamilton and Leclerc have one apiece. If drivers finish level on points, the number of wins becomes the first tie-breaker.
Max Verstappen: Can the Red Bull star defend second place?
Verstappen enters the Sao Paulo weekend as the favourite to finish runner-up, but his position is far from secure. The four-time world champion has 261 points, just two more than Hamilton, and knows that even a small slip could cost him second place.
The Dutchman has enjoyed a strong run of form, winning three of the last four races, including the Mexico City Grand Prix. His ability to recover positions and extract maximum performance from difficult situations makes him a serious threat despite his starting position. However, Verstappen faces a significant challenge at Interlagos after taking a power-unit penalty that puts him at the back of the grid. He will need another exceptional recovery drive if he wants to protect his advantage in the championship.
The Brazilian circuit has offered him opportunities to produce memorable comeback performances before. In 2024, he won from 17th on the grid in wet conditions, while last year he started from the pit lane and finished third. That history will give Red Bull some encouragement, particularly with rain once again threatening to influence Sunday's race.
Lewis Hamilton: Ferrari star has a golden opportunity to take P2
Ferrari's Lewis Hamilton 
Hamilton is just two points behind Verstappen, making the seven-time world champion the closest challenger in the battle for second place.
His first season with Ferrari has had its ups and downs, but the Briton has shown that he can still challenge at the front. His victory earlier in the campaign and recent performances have kept him firmly in contention.
Hamilton also arrives at Interlagos with positive memories. The Brazilian circuit has witnessed some of the most memorable moments of his career, including his dramatic 2021 victory and emotional celebrations in front of the passionate Brazilian crowd.
However, his preparations have not been straightforward. An engine problem during final practice, followed by a power-unit penalty, has left him facing a start from the back of the grid. A strong result could also see him move ahead of Verstappen in the championship standings.
George Russell: Mercedes driver cannot afford another missed opportunity
Russell finds himself third in the battle for P2 with 250 points, 11 behind Verstappen. Although the gap is not insurmountable, the Mercedes driver needs a strong finish to the season to keep his hopes alive.
The Briton has three victories this year, matching Verstappen's tally, and has demonstrated the pace required to compete for the top positions. However, his recent performances have been inconsistent. His difficult Mexico City outing, which included a first-lap deployment issue and a 10-second time penalty, cost him valuable points.
Russell qualified second at Interlagos, just 0.204 seconds behind pole-sitter Lando Norris. That performance initially put him in a strong position to challenge for victory, but a five-place grid penalty has dropped him to seventh.
Unlike Hamilton and Verstappen, Russell will not have to begin from the back of the grid. Nevertheless, he will need to make an immediate impact and take advantage of the Mercedes pace if he wants to close the gap.
Charles Leclerc: Ferrari driver faces an uphill battle
Leclerc is fourth in the fight for second place with 245 points, 16 behind Verstappen. While the gap is larger than that of his three rivals, the Monegasque remains mathematically in contention.
The Ferrari driver has endured a frustrating campaign at times, with missed opportunities and costly battles affecting his consistency. His clash with Hamilton during the Mexico City Grand Prix also attracted attention, with Ferrari team principal Fred Vasseur indicating that discussions would take place within the team. Leclerc qualified fourth at Interlagos, but a 10-place grid penalty means he will start 14th.
That leaves him with a considerable amount of work to do. Unlike Russell, who starts seventh, Leclerc will need to negotiate a crowded midfield before he can challenge for the leading positions. Ferrari's race strategy and tyre management will be crucial, particularly if changing weather conditions create opportunities for an alternative approach.
Rain, penalties and Interlagos: Why the Sao Paulo GP could change everything
The Sao Paulo Grand Prix has a reputation for producing unpredictable races, and the 2026 edition could be no different.
Saturday's qualifying session was heavily affected by rain, with two red flags and a lengthy delay disrupting proceedings. Norris eventually secured pole position with a lap of 1:27.470, beating Russell by 0.204 seconds.
The grid penalties have dramatically reshaped the starting order:
- Lando Norris: Pole position.
- Kimi Antonelli: Second.
- George Russell: Seventh after a five-place penalty.
- Charles Leclerc: 14th after a 10-place penalty.
- Lewis Hamilton: 20th after a power-unit penalty.
- Max Verstappen: 21st after a power-unit penalty.

briefs.headline: Real Madrid stars Rüdiger and Bellingham accused of hitting security staff
briefs.deck: Real Madrid’s 3-0 victory over Valencia was overshadowed by allegations that Antonio Rüdiger slapped a security guard while Jude Bellingham struck another during a half-time tunnel confrontation. However, the referee’s published report made no mention of either player being involved in an assault, leaving the claims unconfirmed and any potential disciplinary action uncertain.
briefs.bodyText:
Real Madrid's 3-0 victory over Valencia at Mestalla was overshadowed by reports of a violent confrontation in the dressing-room tunnel at half-time, with Antonio Rüdiger and Jude Bellingham accused of striking members of the security staff. The allegations, reported by Spanish journalist Nacho Sánchez, have not been confirmed by the referee's published report, which makes no mention of either player being involved in an assault.
Rüdiger and Bellingham accused of striking security staff
Tensions between the two teams had already risen during a heated first half on Saturday, November 7, before a confrontation reportedly broke out as the players made their way towards the dressing rooms. Spanish newspaper 
Sport
 reported: "After referee Hernandez Maeso blew the whistle for the end of the first half and directed the players towards the dressing-room tunnel, a very violent altercation broke out away from the cameras."
According to À Punt journalist Nacho Sánchez, Bellingham and Rüdiger were among the Real Madrid players most heavily involved. Sánchez alleged that the England international struck a security guard, while Rüdiger slapped another member of the security staff.
"Here are more details about the altercation that took place in the dressing-room tunnel. Bellingham assaulted a security guard by striking him, and Rudiger also slapped another security guard. 
The security staff went to the referee, who wrote down everything that happened," Sánchez said.
He added: "This incident is expected to appear in the referee's report after the end of the match, because the security staff informed him of what happened, and he noted down all the details."
Reports also suggested that Bellingham and Éder Militão exchanged provocative remarks with Valencia players as they entered the tunnel, adding to the confrontation. Sánchez's account indicated that the security staff had brought the alleged incidents to the referee's attention.
Referee's report does not mention alleged assaults
The published referee's report, however, has complicated the accounts of what happened. According to 
Mundo Deportivo
, the report documented an altercation involving Valencia sporting director Braulio Vázquez, who allegedly approached the referee and his assistant in an agitated manner. It also referred to police intervention.
Neither Bellingham nor Rüdiger was identified in the report as having assaulted a member of the security staff. This differs from Sánchez's account of the incident, which stated that the security personnel had informed the referee about the alleged strikes and that he had recorded the details.
Further investigations may be required given the limited information and unverified allegations available at the time of writing.
Real Madrid beat Valencia 3-0 at Mestalla
The tunnel controversy followed a match that had already been marked by disputed decisions and confrontations. Real Madrid's opening goal came in the 28th minute, when Federico Valverde scored with a powerful strike from outside the penalty area. The goal followed a free-kick decision that angered the Valencia players, who disputed the referee's decision in the build-up.
Arda Güler doubled Real Madrid's lead eight minutes later, finishing from close range after the ball took a favourable deflection from Bellingham's delivery. Güler then turned provider in the second half, setting up Kylian Mbappé, who rounded the goalkeeper to make it 3-0.
Real Madrid's Arda Guler, left, celebrates after scoring his side's second goal during a Spanish La Liga soccer match between Valencia and Real Madrid in Valencia, Spain, Saturday, Nov. 7, 2026. (AP Photo/Alberto Saiz)
Valencia's afternoon deteriorated further when captain José Gayà was sent off for bringing down Mbappé as the French forward raced towards goal.
The victory extended Real Madrid's winning run to eight matches across all competitions and moved them level with Barcelona on 30 points at the top of La Liga. Valencia remained in the relegation zone.
Real Madrid left Mestalla with three points, but the allegations surrounding the half-time confrontation have shifted attention towards the tunnel incident, with the accounts of Sánchez and the published referee's report leaving important questions about the involvement of Bellingham and Rüdiger unresolved.

briefs.headline: Anuj Shrivatri becomes India’s 100th chess Grandmaster
briefs.deck: The 22-year-old won the 7th ASEAN+ Individual Open chess championship in Ozamiz City, the Philippines
briefs.bodyText:
Anuj Shrivatri on Sunday (November 8, 2026) became India’s 100th chess Grandmaster, by winning the 7th ASEAN+ Individual Open chess championship in Ozamiz City, the Philippines.
The 22-year-old Anuj also became the first GM from Madhya Pradesh. He won the tournament with seven points from nine rounds after suffering a loss in the opening round. His triumph enabled him earn the GM title.
The legendary Viswanathan Anand had become the country’s first Grandmaster in 1988.
The wait for the 100th GM was watched intently after S. Aswath and V.S. Rathanvel recently became the 98th and 99th GMs respectively.

briefs.headline: 'We were 20-30 runs short': India U19 captain Raichandani on defeat against Pakistan
briefs.deck: In a thrilling clash at the ACC Men's U19 Asia Cup, India fell short against arch-rivals Pakistan. Despite a brilliant century from Arjun Rajput, which propelled India to a total of 208 runs, it wasn't enough to secure victory. Hamza Zahoor's remarkable unbeaten century steered Pakistan to a comeback, ultimately overcoming India with 11 balls in hand.
briefs.bodyText:
India Under-19 captain Lakshya Raichandani admitted his side failed to put up a competitive total after Pakistan pulled off a remarkable three-wicket victory in their ACC Men's U19 Asia Cup Group A clash in Oman on Sunday. Despite Arjun Rajput's fighting century, India could not capitalise on a promising recovery, allowing Pakistan to chase down 209 with 11 balls to spare.
Pakistan were in serious trouble at 61/5 before Hamza Zahoor produced a match-winning unbeaten 100 off 108 deliveries. His composed knock, supported by Hasnain Abbas Dar's valuable 38, turned the contest around and handed Pakistan their second consecutive victory in the tournament.
Speaking after the match, Raichandani acknowledged that India were at least 20-30 runs below a competitive total and rued the lack of partnerships around Rajput's innings.
'We were 20-30 runs short': Raichandani admits India's batting failure
India, who elected to bat after winning the toss, suffered an early collapse and were reduced to 42/4. Rajput then took charge with a magnificent 107, keeping India's innings together and helping them recover from a difficult position.
However, the Indian captain felt the team could have added significantly more runs had another batter stayed with Rajput for longer.
"Yeah, they weren't enough. We were 20-30 runs short, but overall there were some good innings from Arjun and a good contribution from KP (Kavya Patel). It was a really good innings, and if someone had stayed there with him (Arjun), it could have been a little bit more total," Raichandani said during the post-match presentation.
India eventually folded for 208 in 46.3 overs, leaving their bowlers with a target that Pakistan managed to overhaul despite losing five wickets early in the chase.
Raichandani admits India could have bowled better
The India skipper also conceded that his bowlers missed opportunities to finish the job after putting Pakistan under considerable pressure. Pakistan were struggling at 61/5, but Zahoor and Dar combined to rebuild the innings and shift the momentum in their team's favour. Raichandani felt India could have been more clinical during that phase.
"Yeah, definitely. We will try to rectify it, and there was a lot of positive from this game. We will try to take that forward. There were some really good efforts. They were 60 for 5. We could have bowled a little bit better, but overall, it was really good," he added.
